newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Top officials dismissed in Rwanda tribunal.
newsitem.headline: Top officials dismissed in Rwanda tribunal.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Wednesday dismissed two top officials of the Rwanda genocide tribunal following a U.N. report that the court was riddled with mismanagement and financial waste.

"The secretary-general decided that the continuation of two officials of the tribunal in their posts would not be in the interests of the United Nations and of the work of the tribunal in a case involving human trategy of incalculable proportion," U.N. spokesman Juan-Carlos Brandt said.

Brandt said Annan had accepted in the "best interests of the United Nations and the tribunal" the resignations of the deputy prosecutor, Honoure Rakotomanana of Madagascar, and the court's registrar, Andonico Adede of Kenya.
Adede will be replaced by Agwu Okali of Nigeria, currently working in the U.N. Habitat office in Nairobi. A new deputy prosecutor has not yet been named.

The tribunal, based in Arusha, Tanzania, is to try leaders alleged to be responsible for the killing by Hutu troops and militia of more than half a million Tutsis and moderate Hutus in Rwanda in 1994.

A report released two weeks ago by Karl Paschke, the U.N. equivalent of an inspector-general, said the court was riddled with administrative mismanagement, unqualified staff, including lawyers, and financial waste. He criticised the deputy prosecutor's office, based in Kigali, Rwanda, and the registrar's office in Arusha.
